_readme: Ground truth for the battle model. Every entry here is a REAL in-game observation,
not a model output. Never edit a number in this file to make a test pass — the whole
point is that the model is fitted to these, not the other way round.
Provenance: the model was recalibrated against 24 in-game samples on 2026-06-27/28
7289025, 62232a3, 243bdfe, 2cc1467). The raw samples were never committed — only
summary numbers inside the commit messages survived. The entries below are the ones
whose INPUTS are stated unambiguously enough to be replayed. The remaining ~15
samples are unrecoverable: their win percentages are quoted but the fleets and stats
behind them are not. Collect them again (see docs/battle-model.md) rather than
confidence: 'observed' = the game reported this number for these exact inputs.
Anything less than 'observed' does not belong in this file.

gate._note: Worst error across the current fixtures is 0.37 pp (physics diff 10). The gate sits just above that so a real regression fails the build while normal float noise does not. Tighten it as better samples arrive.

survivors._status: 8 cases across mirror/reference/race-defense/mathematics/starbase/annihilation, added 2026-09-06 from the reverse-engineering session's harvested data (scripts/battle-harvest/).
_note: Was EMPTY until 2026-09-06. The survivor half of the model was reverse-engineered from
~4200 live-calculator observations across four harvest rounds (see scripts/battle-harvest/
and docs referenced from results.md at the repo root at the time), not guessed — these 8
cases are a representative slice: a no-modifier baseline, the documented 72.66% reference
fight, race defense bonus/malus, mathematics below and above its +-6 gap bracket, a lone
starbase, and the loser-of-a-certain-fight annihilation rule.
Survivor error gate: survivorMaxErrorUnits below. Widen it if a real regression needs it,
never to make a fixture pass.

cases.desc: 1000 destroyers each side, no modifiers — the reference 25% mutual-mirror loss

cases.desc: 1000 destroyers each side, defender +3 race defense — own losses divided by (1 + 0.12*3)
1000 destroyers each side, defender -2 race defense — own losses divided by (1 - 0.12*2), well below the 1-survivor floor but not yet clipped by it
1000 destroyers each side, attacker 4 mathematics ahead (own absolute level, below the +-6 gap bracket)
1000 destroyers each side, attacker 8 mathematics ahead of defender — past the +-6 gap bracket, +25% toughness on top of the absolute-level slope
cases.source: scripts/battle-harvest/results.jsonl, round 1, block 6-math-grid; this same case caught the original 'is it a gap or an absolute level' confusion resolved in round 3

cases.desc: level-11 starbase alone (CV 342) defending against 100 attacking destroyers (CV 300) -- the defending starbase survives a fraction of its CV. NOTE: the live calculator's own on-screen 'Starbase' row for this field shows 8.85, which is NOT this fraction (0.4152) nor CV directly (142) -- it is that same 142 remaining CV re-expressed as a fractional 'effective level' by linearly interpolating between the two integer starbase levels whose table CV brackets it (level 8 = 99 CV, level 9 = 150 CV -> 8 + (142-99)/(150-99) = 8.84, matching the displayed 8.85 to within rounding). The 0.4152 checked here is the actual CV fraction the model computes; converting it to that display format is a UI concern, not a model one.
cases.source: scripts/battle-harvest/results.jsonl, round 1, block 3-sb-alone; same case as the win% fixture above

cases.desc: 2 attacking destroyers vs 1 defending destroyer — a deterministic (100/0) same-type fight; the loser is wiped to exactly 0, not the partial loss the CV-ratio formula alone would give

50 destroyers + level-9 starbase defending against 100 destroyers. The starbase survives at displayed level 6.11; leaving its toughness out of the loss fraction wiped it (and all but one destroyer) (calculator shows the starbase row as an effective level; 6.11 converted to a CV fraction here)

20 cruisers + level-15 starbase defending against 1000 destroyers. Displayed starbase level 9.86; the starbase toughness has to be in the denominator for it to survive at all (calculator shows the starbase row as an effective level; 9.86 converted to a CV fraction here)
defender with a ~x2 toughness multiplier facing 2.66x its toughness in enemy CV: the cap comes after the multiplier, so it is wiped to 1 ship (the old cap-first rule kept 54% of it)
cases.source: in-game battle calculator, 2026-10-04 sweep through the hub (/root/calc-sweep case X1-197)

gate._note: Worst error across these 8 cases should be near-exact (<0.01) since they come directly from the same data the formula was fit to; 0.5 leaves headroom for float noise without hiding a real regression.
